text:
deploy-bot: Heads-up: rolling a CONFIG-ONLY change during change window 23:00-01:00 UTC. Canary policy: 5% for 20m -> evaluate -> 25% -> full. Config diff: routing.policy.global_weight: 0.88 -> 0.76; batching.max_requests: 18 -> 12; batching.max_tokens: 2300 -> 1600; request.timeout_ms: 25000 -> 35000. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/commit/def456. Automated rollback rules posted in PR. Watch keys: per-tenant p99, error_rate, kvcache_hit_rate. Manual rollback criteria: error_rate >0.4% sustained 5m or p99 +250ms sustained 10m. Auto-unpin if gateway_errors >0.35%.

maria.g: ack. I'll be online from 22:45 to monitor. Note: two enterprise tenants still pinned to heavyweight variant; they shouldn't be affected but I'll double-check their traffic routing.

samk: confirm: this is global routing weight nudge, not per-tenant, right? Concerned about PLG cohorts that rely on the heavy variant for quality.

deploy-bot: correct — global weight change applies to unpinned traffic only. Pinned tenant routing takes precedence, pinned tenants unaffected.

oliver: smaller batches + lower max_tokens might increase KV cache churn and cold-start misses. Any warmup job? We should run a soft-warmup for slim variant before expanding.

maria.g: good call. I'll trigger the warmup job 15m before promoting beyond canary. Also adding kvcache query alert threshold: if hit_rate drops below 0.90 for 5m, consider throttling rollout.

qa-bot: quick check snippet to watch cache and errors:
```
# run in ops shell
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/series?k=kvcache.hit_rate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MON" | jq .value
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/series?k=request.errors" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MON" | jq .value
```
Expected: kvcache_hit_rate >= 0.92 pre-change.

oncall-amber: I'll be oncall in #eng-oncall. If deploy-bot flags rollback, ping me; I'll authorize immediate rollback if thresholds met. Manual rollback threshold set to error_rate >0.35% for 5m AND ops signoff.

samk: I'll run prompt-set A quality checks against a sampled 1k requests from canary to look for regressions. Share results in 15m.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 23:06 UTC (5%). Initial metrics: error_rate 0.01%, p99 +18ms, kvcache_hit_rate 0.94. Monitoring.

deploy-bot: Canary at 12m: stable. No gateway errors. Promoting to 25% at 23:32 UTC.

maria.g: warmup for slim variant kicked at 23:28. Observed small spike in kvcache misses for 3m, recovered. Good.

samk: QA results from prompt-set A: small delta in relevancy for <2% of samples, within expected tolerances. No major quality regressions.

deploy-bot: Promotion to 25% complete. Monitoring 25m before full rollout. Rolling log: https://console.redwood/logs/deploy/def456

oncall-amber: staying until 00:45 UTC. If we see sustained error_rate >0.3% escalate to full rollback. Otherwise proceed.

maria.g: release note draft:
"Config-only: routing weight smoothing (global), reduced batching sizes and token limits for tail-latency stabilization, increased request timeout to absorb slower backends. Expected outcome: slightly lower cost + improved p95 stability; monitor p99 for regressions."

oliver: thumbs up. If kvcache_hit_rate dips again, hold promotion and run cache-warmup with synthetic load.

deploy-bot: At 00:10 UTC promoted to 100%. Final checks green. Closing thread; tag release notes and changelog. If anyone sees unexpected tenant issues, please open an incident and reference commit def456.
